To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) plant closures are more likely to occur in the EU countries that have the highest levels of government subsidies, and (ii) plant closures are less likely to occur in EU countries where labour markets are characterized by high levels of union membership.

the closure decisions of multinational firms are influenced by the economies of scale and scope of the plants, the relative labour costs of the countries concerned, the degree of unionization in the countries, the relative size of the plants, and the political context of each country.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the closure of plants in multinational firms operating in the EU.
the impact of the closure of a plant in one EU country on the plants of a multiplant manufacturing firm in another EU country.
the impact of internationalization on the management and closure of multiplant manufacturing companies in the EU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the closure of a plant in one country and the opening of a plant in another are not necessarily incompatible.
plant closures are a complex phenomenon and the decision‐making processes are difficult to understand.
plant economies of scale are the dominant force encouraging the closure of plants in the EU.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plant closures in our study were not driven by any single factor, and that the decision to close a plant is a very complex one.

, although the plant economies of scale and the national characteristics of the labour force can be important in explaining plant closures in multiplant firms, managers need to take account of the political environment in which the plant is located.
, although plant economies of scale and labour cost differences are the dominant determinants of closure, the closure decision is also strongly affected by the political context of a country.
The main takeaway from our work is that
managers of multinational firms need to be aware of the potential political consequences of their decisions to close plants.
the decision to close one or more plants is not necessarily an easy one for multinational firms.
managers need to be careful when making closure decisions in the context of multiplant manufacturing firms.
